title: Generational River Cleanup Crew Dilemma

scenario.title: Generational River Cleanup Crew Dilemma
scenario.setting: A sun-bleached wooden dock straddling a shallow, trash-lined creek in western Pennsylvania. The volunteer cleanup crew has split into two groups: a small core of long-time organizers and a large cohort of first-time teen volunteers. Tensions simmer as the two sides clash over cleanup priorities and group dynamics.

characters.name: Javi
characters.tendencies: Strictly tracks trash collection numbers and argues for faster, more efficient cleanup routes over casual volunteer chat.

characters.name: Marisol
characters.tendencies: Amplifies quieter volunteer voices, shares personal creek restoration stories, and pushes for inclusive group decisions.

characters.name: Theo
characters.tendencies: Manages heavy cleanup equipment, mentors new teen volunteers, and feels out of place between the crew’s conflicting factions.

turns.name: Javi
turns.text:
Cut the small talk—we’ve only tallied 13 full trash bags in the past hour, and we’re already trailing the efficient route I drafted by 20 minutes. If we stick to the mapped upstream trash cluster instead of loitering by the dock posts, we can make up that lost ground before the high tide pushes more debris out into the cove.
[slams his waterproof trash count tracker onto the sun-bleached dock rail, grabs a heavy-duty trash grabber, and strides toward the tangled pile of discarded bait buckets and plastic sheeting bobbing just offshore]

turns.name: Marisol
turns.text:
I want to shout out Lila, who’s been quietly pointing out all the hidden litter spots along the back creek bend every time we pause. Three years ago, my abuela and I pulled a rusted lawnmower out of that exact same bend, and seeing how much less heavy trash clogs it now makes me hope we can expand this work with local students. Let’s make sure every single person here gets a chance to share their ideas for how to grow our volunteer group.
[Hands a branded trash grabber and a stack of student volunteer sign-up sheets to the shy teen Lila, then gestures for the scattered cleanup crew to huddle closer to brainstorm together.]

turns.name: Theo
turns.text:
Alright, y’all, let’s pause the infighting for five minutes. The eastern dock edge has a pile of broken fishing floats and chemical containers that need the heavy-duty grabber, so the crew that’s been hogging the small tongs can step aside for that. The west bank’s storm drains are clogged with plastic bags, so don’t drag your feet tackling those once we split up.
[Slings the heavy industrial cleanup grabber’s strap over one broad shoulder, kicking a crumpled potato chip bag out of the way of the dock’s wobbly plank stairs.]

turns.name: Javi
turns.text:
Cut the five-minute pause right now—we’re already 20 minutes behind my drafted efficient route, and we’ve only tallied 13 full trash bags in the past hour. That fishing float pile and casual shoutouts can wait until we hit our assigned coverage targets first. I spotted the cluster of hidden litter Lila pointed out just further up the back creek bend, let’s move now instead of wasting time on formalities.
[Javi grabs his heavy-duty trash grabber from his tool belt and strides purposefully toward the back creek bend, ignoring the calls to halt for the eastern dock float pile inspection.

turns.name: Marisol
turns.text:
Three years ago, I was the harried volunteer rushing straight through these exact stretches, blind to every piece of trash tucked under the dock’s rotting pilings and tucked in the creek’s overgrown banks. Lila’s been doing the quiet, careful work that actually makes this cleanup count, and I think we should shift a few folks to join her instead of only fixating on our tally numbers right now.
[I kneel to pluck a crumpled plastic soda bottle wedged between two weathered dock slats, holding it up to gesture toward the overgrown back creek bend where Lila’s crouched sorting hidden trash.]

turns.name: Theo
turns.text:
First off, Lila, that sharp eye for hidden litter has saved us so much hassle—thank you for pointing all those tucked-away bits out. Javi, I hear your push to stick to your drafted route, but that pile of chemical containers by the east dock can’t wait; we’ve got to bag those safely first to keep everyone out of harm’s way. Let’s split the crew quick: half of you wrap up the full trash bags we’ve already filled, and the rest follow me over to handle that hazardous pile right now.
[Grabs a pair of thick, puncture-resistant work gloves from his utility belt, then hefts a roll of extra-heavy plastic trash bags over one shoulder to head toward the eastern dock edge.]

dm_opening: DM opening: the cast gathers around a question the scene has been carrying for a year.
dm_closing: DM closing: the Javi holds the line; the next session's hook waits at the door.
